subject: Computational bottleneck for large n, but low-dimensional latent field

messages.author: 26d91fa89845f9cd
messages.subject: Computational bottleneck for large n, but low-dimensional latent field
parts:
Hi all,

I am fitting a multivariate spatial model with three responses, x (Gamma), y (Gamma),  and z (Bernoulli). The number of spatial locations is large (n ~ 1,000,000), but the range of the spatial effects is large relative to location density, so I can use a low-dimensional latent fields (k = mesh$n ~ 2,500). 

Vector x is fully populated, but y and z and many missing values (NAs), with around 20,000 entries populated and the rest NAs. 

The goal of the analysis is to get posterior means and sd's for y and z at all of the locations, including the NAs. Actually, I eventually want posterior means and sd's of y*z, but perhaps I'll cross that bridge next.

If I truncate my observations/locations to only complete observations across x, y, z with the same mesh (so n ~20,000, but still k ~2,500), the analysis is very fast, completing in around 10 minutes. But if I include all values, the analysis is very slow. I only attempted it once, and my laptop crashed after over 8 hours of runtime. I am running with 'verbose = T', and strangely the longest stage is the preliminary stage, before inla() starts printing out gradients, likelihood evaluations, etc. The text it pauses on is:

Strategy = [DEFAULT]
    Mode..................... [Classic]
    Sparse-matrix library.... [taucs]
    OpenMP strategy.......... [huge]
    num.threads.............. [4:1]
    blas.num.threads......... [1]

It sat here for multiple hours. This huge difference in runtime contradicts my knowledge of INLA, as I thought the primary bottleneck was Cholesky's of k x k precision matrices, and k has not changed. I have set quantiles = NULL and control.predictor(quantiles = NULL) to try to avoid any unnecessary computing there.

Any thoughts on the computational bottleneck here? Things I can do to speed it up?

Below is the R code for the INLA infrastructure. Thanks in advance.

#############################
me = 0.4
mesh = inla.mesh.2d(loc.domain = coord, max.edge = c(me, 5*me)
                    , offset = c(me,6*me)
                    )
mesh$n # around 2,500


A = inla.spde.make.A(mesh, coord)

spdey = inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh = mesh,
                           prior.sigma = c(2, 0.01),
                           prior.range = c(1, 0.01))

spdex = inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh = mesh,
                            prior.sigma = c(1.2, 0.01),
                            prior.range = c(1, 0.01))

spdez = inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh = mesh,
                           prior.sigma = c(3, 0.5),
                           prior.range = c(1, 0.01))



stacky = inla.stack(data = list(Y = cbind(y, NA, NA), link = 1),
                    A = list(A),
                    effects = list(list(inty = 1, s1 = 1:mesh$n)))

stackx = inla.stack(data = list(Y = cbind(NA, x.hat, NA), link = 1),
                    A = list(A),
                    effects = list(list(intx = 1, s12 = 1:mesh$n, s2 = 1:mesh$n)))

stackz = inla.stack(data = list(Y = cbind(NA, NA, z), link = 1),
                    A = list(A),
                    effects = list(list(intz = 1, s13 = 1:mesh$n, s3 = 1:mesh$n)))

stack = inla.stack(stacky, stackx, stackz)

form = Y ~ 0 + inty + intx + intz +
  f(s1, model = spdey) +
  f(s12, copy = "s1", fixed = F) +
  f(s2, model = spdex) +
  f(s13, copy = "s1", fixed = F) +
  f(s3, model = spdez)

mod = inla(formula = form, family = c("Gamma", "Gamma", "Binomial"),
           data = inla.stack.data(stack),
           control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stack),
                                    link = link,
                                    quantiles = NULL),
           control.inla = list(strategy = 'gaussian', int.strategy = 'eb'),
           quantiles = NULL,
           verbose = T)

parts:
In addition, you need to correct the link=… values in the stack constructions; you have link=1 for all three, but should have link=1, link=2, and link=3. Otherwise, it will apply the log-link also to the Bernoulli case, which clearly could cause problems (an also be wrong).

Finn
